scope: make the keyword schema linker stop rescanning the whole snapshot per candidate
behaviour-preserving: same rules, same confidence values, same ordering
no new database support, no real model calls, no concurrency change

profiling.method: cProfile around SchemaLinkingNode.execute on a synthetic SQLite schema, three executes per measurement, 1k and 10k tables with 12 columns each

share_of_remaining_time.SchemaNameIndex.__init__: 0.369 s of 0.879 s profiled (about 123 ms per request): building the index is now the cost

changes.what: one linear pass per request builds name lookups; the four matching rules are answered from dictionaries plus C-level str.find scans
rules_preserved: table: exact 1.0, case-insensitive 0.95, comment containment 0.7, substring either way 0.65
column: exact 1.0, case-insensitive 0.95, comment containment 0.75, candidate inside name 0.65, name inside candidate 0.6
changes.ordering: descending confidence, then schema order; because the confidences strictly decrease, keeping the maximum per name reproduces the old first-match elif chain
edge_cases_found: threshold 0.0 returned every table and column with confidence 0.0 in the old scan; the index reproduces that explicitly
an empty candidate matches everything at 0.65 through Python's '' in s semantics; kept

changes.what: build the index once per execute and pass it to both _match_schema passes, the reverse scan and the multi-table hint; _all_table_matches/_all_column_matches removed

pipeline_1k.instrument: scripts/scale_load, pipeline scenario, 15 requests, concurrency 1, fresh fixture per run

pipeline_10k.instrument: scripts/scale_load, pipeline scenario, 6 requests, concurrency 1, per-stage durations captured from the stage events
pipeline_10k.reading: the retrieve stage drops 877 -> 569 ms (-35%); generate/validate/execute move by +-90 ms between runs with unchanged code, so the 192 ms total delta understates the retrieve win and is inside session noise

keyword_retrieve_scenario.reading: the retriever's own keyword path is cheap; the O(tables) cost lived in the Phase-2 fallback scan inside SchemaLinkingNode

measurements.session_noise_warning: absolute numbers moved by more than 2x between the stage-51 session and this one on the same machine (an unchanged 10k pipeline measured 1307 ms then and 3059 ms now), so only the paired before/after runs above are used as evidence

tests_added.method: a verbatim copy of the replaced loops is kept in the test module and compared against the index over randomised schemas, candidates, thresholds and queries, including exact ordering
cases: 12 seeds x 9 thresholds for table matching
12 seeds x 9 thresholds for column matching
8 seeds x 8 queries for the reverse table-name scan
8 seeds x 8 queries for the direct keyword fallback
explicit cases: reuse, ordering, comment case folding, parts shorter than three characters, empty candidate, snapshot not mutated

verification.ruff: ruff check app/ tests/ -> All checks passed
verification.mypy: mypy app/ -> no issues in 192 source files

full_suite.note: both failures are in the known Windows-only set; the third test from that set (test_concurrent_request_audits_keep_their_own_tokens) passed this run, i.e. it is timing-flaky rather than deterministic

corrections: stage-51 recorded 'keyword retrieval is still an O(tables) scan, about 0.9 s at 10k' without a measurement behind it; measured now, the pipeline retrieve stage was 877 ms at 10k and the name-matching scan is about 490 ms of that, while SchemaRetriever.retrieve alone is 10 ms
not_covered: the index is rebuilt per request: at 10k that build is 123 ms of the 125 ms node time, so the per-request cost is now linear-but-single-pass rather than solved
the rest of the 569 ms retrieve stage at 10k is _build_filtered_schema, _filter_schema, foreign-key expansion and result shaping; not touched this round
synthetic vocabulary only: the fixture reuses the same column names across tables, so unique-name counts are not representative of a real 10k-table warehouse
SQLite only; PostgreSQL/MySQL linking paths were not measured
the differential tests prove equality with the previous implementation, not that the previous rules are the right ranking
